subject: Henry Clifton Sorby (1826-1908)
gate: NAMESAKE-GUARD-实测.md 3-way test: (1) middle name 'Clifton' present IN THE NAME; (2) F.R.S. or F.G.S. beside the byline; (3) source is an 1850-1908 learned-society serial. Hit ANY ONE = target. Red line: pre-1850 material signed only 'Henry Sorby' is treated as the FATHER.
how_exclusion_was_decided: For every excluded person I record which of the three inclusion criteria FAILS. A person is excluded only when ALL THREE fail (or when the red line applies). Criterion 3 is the weakest discriminator because it is a container test, not a person test - it is never used ALONE to exclude, only to confirm.

false_positive_mechanisms_found_during_t.mechanism: criterion 1 read as 'the string Clifton appears in the document' instead of 'Clifton is the subject's middle name'
false_positive_mechanisms_found_during_t.evidence: Staged file A8 (Proc. Roy. Soc. vol. 26, Sorby's own text) reads 'a very similar addition was made to a microscope in Professor Clifton's laboratory at Oxford' - that is Robert Bellamy Clifton, the Oxford physicist. The same surname also appears in G. G. Stokes's companion paper in the same IA item. A document-level 'Clifton' test therefore returns TRUE for reasons that have nothing to do with the subject's identity.
false_positive_mechanisms_found_during_t.fix: Criterion 1 must be evaluated on the byline/name string only, never on the document body.
